To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the probability of having a particular health status in the next period and the distribution function for lifetime healthcare costs can be estimated for the whole population, by combining a morbidity classification with stochastic microsimulation.

the mean lifetime cost for a woman in the sample was €111,935, while for a man it was €81,565, and that women spent a longer period of their lives in a chronic disease state (28.41 versus 21.9 years).

the probability of having a particular health status in the next year can be obtained from a stationary Markov Chain, that the probability of a particular morbidity pattern for a given age can be obtained by multiplying probabilities of the health status in the previous year, and that the distribution function of lifetime costs can be obtained by adding the distribution of costs in the next year to the lifetime cost distribution of the previous year.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a methodology to simulate the evolution of the health status of the individuals in a given population, and to estimate the distribution of the healthcare costs of the individuals in the population over their lifetimes.
a more efficient and effective management of chronic diseases in a time horizon of 10–15 years.

the development of a methodology to estimate the future evolution of morbidity in a population, and the associated healthcare costs, using a longitudinal perspective to the chronic disease management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CRG classification system is a useful tool for the analysis of healthcare costs and future morbidity patterns, and can be used as an instrument for decision-making and policy evaluation.
the model presented here is useful to identify the most vulnerable groups of patients in the population, and to predict their future morbidity evolution and healthcare costs.
a better understanding of the evolution of health conditions over time would help in the design and implementation of more efficient and effective healthcare policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CRG classification system, when combined with a stochastic simulation model and longitudinal data, can be used to estimate lifetime morbidity patterns and costs for a whole population.
a small number (1.7%) of individuals (the most complex) account for 50% of the total costs.

, by using this methodology, we could obtain the expected costs and the expected morbidity patterns in the future for a population, and we could identify the groups of individuals that are likely to consume the largest part of the resources in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CRG model is a useful tool to predict the evolution of chronic disease and healthcare resource consumption in the long term.
the lifetime cost distribution function is an essential tool to estimate the impact of healthcare policies on the population.
a significant proportion of the population (around a third) will spend a large part of their life with a chronic condition.
